11. COMMUNITY EVENTS UPDATE 
 
Ms. Weber announced a Job Fair at the Bonsall Community Center, on March 29th, sponsored by 
the School District , providing the opportunity to showcase Rainbow as a community partner. 
Member Kozak suggested internships , in addition to requesting volunteers for these events. 
Member Johnson announced that the Bonsall School District is currently working on an internship 
program.   Mr. Wiley reported that the District has an internship program and has two interns, 
currently.  The District is also looking into a program that transitions military personnel. The District 
is in support of participating as a partner for internships .  Ms. Weber added that Rainbow staff 
have also visited classrooms to share information about careers in the water industry.  Ms. Weber 
is in constant communication with several local schools, looking for the opport unity to make an 
impact and relay examples of practical applications.   
 
The Avocado Festival will be held on April 13, 2025, and staff plans to attend to share information 
and an interactive game to teach “What Not To Flush.”  High school students can earn community 
service hours by volunteering their time. Information about this event is in this month’s newsletter. 
Ms. Weber encouraged Committee and staff volunteers to donate their time.   
 
A Wildfire Symposium will be held on May 3, 2025, at the Fallbrook Union High School. It is a free 
event, at which Rainbow Water will host an information table.  Also in May, the District will be 
offering field trips for students. This will be a collaborative effort with the City of Oceanside, touring 
the San Luis Rey Wastewater Treatment Plant.  
 
 
12. NEWSLETTER CONTENT PLANNING 
 
The March newsletter was distributed last week, and highlights how to fix a leak, “Water Wise for 
Life” spring planting tips, collaboration of local water agencies to boost efficiency, and upcoming 
community events.  Instructional videos on how to locate a water meter , how to find a leak, and 
how to turn off a water meter were shared with the Committee. These videos were created in -
house, by staff. The April newsletter will include information on the “Water Wise for Life”tips, Earth 
Day, Grants awarded to Rainbow Water, the Wildfire Symposium, and construction/traffic notice.   
The May edition will include information on “Drinking Water Week,”  a water quality update, the 
Avocado Festival recap, information about an upcoming blood drive, and a  highlight on the 
District’s pump stations.  Mr. Wiley added that staff will have the opportunity to speak with Darrell 
Issa and relay our needs for grants to fund wildfire preparedness infrastructure and pipeline  
replacements. Staff anticipates that some funding related to wildfire relief may be obtained at the 
state level.  
 
Chairman Shute asked if staff can measure traffic QR codes in newsletters. Staff answered that, 
due to limited resources, we do not. However , we do receive data from MWD reflecting 
participation in programs such as Flume. Member Kozak noted that he had received positive 
feedback from members of the community regarding all the District’s efforts to interact  with the 
community.
